seaCold.name: Herring
seaCold.note: The silver of the North Sea. Whole towns rose and fell with its shoals.

seaCold.name: Mackerel
seaCold.note: Comes inshore in summer in hungry, flashing packs.

seaCold.name: Cod
seaCold.note: Salted and dried, it fed sailors and Lent for a thousand years.

seaCold.name: Haddock
seaCold.note: Look for the dark thumbprint behind the gills.

seaCold.name: Saithe
seaCold.note: Also called coalfish, for its sooty back.

seaCold.name: Plaice
seaCold.note: Lies flat on the sand with both eyes on one side.

seaCold.name: Gurnard
seaCold.note: It grunts when you lift it out of the water.

seaCold.name: Spurdog
seaCold.note: A small shark that hunts in packs. Its rough skin was used as sandpaper.

seaCold.name: Ling
seaCold.note: A long, lean cousin of the cod, dried hard as a board for winter.

seaCold.name: Conger eel
seaCold.note: Hides in wrecks and rocks by day and hunts at night.

seaCold.name: Lobster
seaCold.note: Blue-black in the sea. It only turns red in the pot.

seaCold.name: Crab
seaCold.note: Walks sideways into the pot and can't find the way out.

seaCold.name: Halibut
seaCold.note: The giant of the flatfish. One can feed a village.

seaWarm.name: Sardine
seaWarm.note: Packed in salt by the barrel and carried inland on mules.

seaWarm.name: Anchovy
seaWarm.note: Drawn up to lamps at night. Its salted guts made Roman garum.

seaWarm.name: Gilt-head bream
seaWarm.note: Named for the gold bar between its eyes. Romans farmed it in ponds.

seaWarm.name: Red mullet
seaWarm.note: Rich Romans paid fortunes for big ones and watched them change colour.

seaWarm.name: Grey mullet
seaWarm.note: Jumps clean out of the water when something startles it.

seaWarm.name: Sea bass
seaWarm.note: The wolf of the sea, hunting through the surf at dusk.

seaWarm.name: Dentex
seaWarm.note: Big teeth, a bad temper and very good eating.

seaWarm.name: Cuttlefish
seaWarm.note: Squirts ink when caught. The ink was used for writing and drawing.

seaWarm.name: Octopus
seaWarm.note: Crawls into clay pots to hide, so fishers lower pots just for it.

seaWarm.name: Moray eel
seaWarm.note: Romans kept them in garden ponds, and some owners doted on them.

seaWarm.name: Bluefin tuna
seaWarm.note: Caught in great mazes of net along the coast each spring.

seaWarm.name: Swordfish
seaWarm.note: Hunted with harpoons from small boats in the Strait of Messina.

seaEastAsia.name: Red sea bream
seaEastAsia.note: Madai: the fish for weddings, new year and every celebration.

seaEastAsia.name: Japanese mackerel
seaEastAsia.note: Salted, grilled and eaten with rice on ordinary days.

seaEastAsia.name: Pacific saury
seaEastAsia.note: Sanma: the taste of autumn, grilled until the skin crackles.

seaEastAsia.name: Flounder
seaEastAsia.note: Buries itself in sand with only its eyes showing.

seaEastAsia.name: Yellowtail
seaEastAsia.note: Its name changes as it grows, like a person's in old Japan.

seaEastAsia.name: Squid
seaEastAsia.note: Rises to the lamps hung over the boats on summer nights.

seaEastAsia.name: Pufferfish
seaEastAsia.note: Fugu. Deadly unless a trained hand cuts it.

seaEastAsia.name: Octopus
seaEastAsia.note: Crawls into clay pots to hide, so fishers lower pots just for it.

seaEastAsia.name: Bluefin tuna
seaEastAsia.note: Caught in great mazes of net along the coast each spring.

seaEastAsia.name: Lantern bream
seaEastAsia.note: A red sea bream with a copper cheek and three rows of pearl scales. It turns on its side just before it dives.

seaTropical.name: Scad
seaTropical.note: Small, plentiful and dried on racks along every reef coast.

seaTropical.name: Snapper
seaTropical.note: Bright red and always welcome at the market.

seaTropical.name: Parrotfish
seaTropical.note: Grinds coral with its beak. Much of the white sand is its work.

seaTropical.name: Milkfish
seaTropical.note: Raised in seaside ponds in Java and the Philippines for centuries.

seaTropical.name: Flying fish
seaTropical.note: Glides over the waves on its fins to escape whatever is chasing it.

seaTropical.name: Trevally
seaTropical.note: Hunts in gangs along the reef edge and pulls like a horse.

seaTropical.name: Barracuda
seaTropical.note: All teeth. Big ones can make you ill to eat.

seaTropical.name: Mahi-mahi
seaTropical.note: Flashes gold, green and blue, and fades the moment it's landed.

seaTropical.name: Moray eel
seaTropical.note: Lives in a hole in the reef and comes out after dark.

seaTropical.name: Octopus
seaTropical.note: Fishers lure it out of the reef with a cowrie shell on a line.

seaTropical.name: Spiny lobster
seaTropical.note: No big claws. It walks out at night to feed.

seaTropical.name: Grouper
seaTropical.note: Lives for decades in one cave and fights all the way to the boat.

seaTropical.name: Sailfish
seaTropical.note: The fastest fish in the sea. Its great sail folds flat when it swims.

seaTropical.name: Blue pennant
seaTropical.note: A sailfish with a tall blue sail edged in silver. A flash above a rain-darkened sea gives it away.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Bonga shad
seaAtlanticTropical.note: The everyday fish of this coast, smoked by the basketful over clay ovens.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Sardinella
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Comes inshore in great shoals when the cold water wells up.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Grey mullet
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Jumps clean out of the water when something startles it.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Tilapia
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Plentiful in the brackish lagoons behind the bar.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Croaker
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Drums with its swim bladder; you can hear it grunt as it comes up.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Snapper
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Bright red and always welcome at the market.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Grouper
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Lives for decades in one cave and fights all the way to the boat.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Barracuda
seaAtlanticTropical.note: All teeth. Big ones can make you ill to eat.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Swimming crab
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Scuttles into the baited traps set in the lagoon mud.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Pink shrimp
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Sold dried by the measure in every market inland.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Octopus
seaAtlanticTropical.note: Fishers lure it out of the reef with a cowrie shell on a line.

seaAtlanticTropical.name: Tarpon
seaAtlanticTropical.note: A great silver fish that throws itself clear of the water when hooked.

riverTemperate.name: Roach
riverTemperate.note: The everyday fish of English and German rivers, red-finned and bony.

riverTemperate.name: Gudgeon
riverTemperate.note: Tiny and greedy. Children caught them by the dozen and fried them whole.

riverTemperate.name: Perch
riverTemperate.note: Hunts in little gangs. Mind the spiky fin on its back.

riverTemperate.name: Bream
riverTemperate.note: Slimy, bronze and slow. Monasteries kept them in their fish ponds.

riverTemperate.name: Chub
riverTemperate.note: Eats almost anything, cherries and beetles included.

riverTemperate.name: Tench
riverTemperate.note: The doctor fish. Its slime was said to heal other fish.

riverTemperate.name: Brown trout
riverTemperate.note: Rises to flies in the evening, in clear and quick water.

riverTemperate.name: Barbel
riverTemperate.note: Feels for food along the bottom with four whiskers.

riverTemperate.name: Zander
riverTemperate.note: Hunts in the half-light with big, glassy eyes.

riverTemperate.name: Eel
riverTemperate.note: Nobody knew where eels were born. Rents were paid in them by the thousand.

riverTemperate.name: Crayfish
riverTemperate.note: Comes to a basket baited with meat after dark.

riverTemperate.name: Lamprey
riverTemperate.note: An English king is said to have died of eating too many.

riverTemperate.name: Pike
riverTemperate.note: Waits among the reeds and strikes like an arrow.

riverTemperate.name: Sturgeon
riverTemperate.note: Armoured, ancient and full of caviar. Kings claimed every one.

riverTemperate.name: Copper pike
riverTemperate.note: A long pike with pale flank spots and fins the colour of fallen beech leaves. Watch for its second leap.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Yellow perch
riverNorthAmerica.note: Schools in the shallows and bites all year, even through the ice.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Sunfish
riverNorthAmerica.note: Round as a coin and guards its nest in the sand.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Largemouth bass
riverNorthAmerica.note: Lurks under logs and lily pads and strikes at anything.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Walleye
riverNorthAmerica.note: Its eyes shine like a cat's in the dark.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Channel catfish
riverNorthAmerica.note: Finds its food at night by taste, all over its whiskered skin.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Shad
riverNorthAmerica.note: Runs up the rivers each spring in shoals so big they fed whole towns.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Eel
riverNorthAmerica.note: Caught in stone weirs and smoked for the winter.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Crayfish
riverNorthAmerica.note: Hides under stones by day and walks into baited traps at night.

riverNorthAmerica.name: Sturgeon
riverNorthAmerica.note: Can live longer than a person. Some leap clear of the water.

riverCold.name: Grayling
riverCold.note: Has a tall, flag-like back fin, and smells faintly of thyme.

riverCold.name: Whitefish
riverCold.note: Netted under the ice and frozen on the shore by the sledge-load.

riverCold.name: Perch
riverCold.note: Hunts in little gangs. Mind the spiky fin on its back.

riverCold.name: Arctic char
riverCold.note: Its belly turns flame red when it spawns.

riverCold.name: Pike
riverCold.note: Waits among the reeds and strikes like an arrow.

riverCold.name: Burbot
riverCold.note: The only cod of fresh water. It spawns under the ice in midwinter.

riverCold.name: Lake trout
riverCold.note: Lives in deep, cold lakes and grows old and large there.

riverCold.name: Salmon
riverCold.note: Climbs waterfalls to reach the stream where it hatched.

riverEastAsia.name: Crucian carp
riverEastAsia.note: Funa. Packed in rice to ferment for years into narezushi.

riverEastAsia.name: Ayu
riverEastAsia.note: Fishers send trained cormorants after it by firelight.

riverEastAsia.name: Loach
riverEastAsia.note: Wriggles through the mud of rice paddies.

riverEastAsia.name: Freshwater shrimp
riverEastAsia.note: Scooped from the weeds and simmered in soy.

riverEastAsia.name: Yamame trout
riverEastAsia.note: Lives high in mountain streams and darts like a shadow.

riverEastAsia.name: Mandarin fish
riverEastAsia.note: Poets praised it fat in spring, when the peach blossom falls.

riverEastAsia.name: Snakehead
riverEastAsia.note: Breathes air and can live for days out of water.

riverEastAsia.name: Eel
riverEastAsia.note: Grilled in high summer to keep up your strength.

riverEastAsia.name: Carp
riverEastAsia.note: If it leaps the Dragon Gate falls, the story says, it becomes a dragon.

riverEastAsia.name: Grass carp
riverEastAsia.note: Grazes on water plants like a cow, and grows as big.

riverEastAsia.name: Catfish
riverEastAsia.note: In Japan the great namazu under the earth was said to cause earthquakes.

riverEastAsia.name: Reed ghost
riverEastAsia.note: A pale carp with honey-coloured fins. In rain the tail is often the only part you see.

riverDry.name: Tilapia
riverDry.note: Keeps its eggs and young safe in its mouth.

riverDry.name: Barbel
riverDry.note: Feels for food along the bottom with four whiskers.

riverDry.name: Elephantfish
riverDry.note: Its long nose feels the mud, and it talks to its kind in faint electric pulses.

riverDry.name: Pufferfish
riverDry.note: Swells up like a ball. Egyptians drew it floating on tomb walls.

riverDry.name: Catfish
riverDry.note: Swims upside down to feed on the surface.

riverDry.name: Electric catfish
riverDry.note: Gives a hard shock. Ancient doctors tried it as a cure for pain.

riverDry.name: Nile perch
riverDry.note: Huge and silver. Egyptians wrapped some as mummies.

riverSouthAsia.name: Rohu
riverSouthAsia.note: The fish of a Bengali wedding, cooked in mustard.

riverSouthAsia.name: Catla
riverSouthAsia.note: Big-headed and fast-growing, raised in village tanks.

riverSouthAsia.name: Hilsa
riverSouthAsia.note: Swims upriver with the monsoon rains. Bengal waits all year for it.

riverSouthAsia.name: Murrel
riverSouthAsia.note: A snakehead that breathes air and survives dry ponds in the mud.

riverSouthAsia.name: Walking catfish
riverSouthAsia.note: Can wriggle over wet ground to the next pond.

riverSouthAsia.name: Freshwater prawn
riverSouthAsia.note: A giant river prawn with long, blue claws.

riverSouthAsia.name: Mahseer
riverSouthAsia.note: The tiger of the river, famous for the fight it puts up.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Barb
riverSoutheastAsia.note: Silver, quick and turned into fish paste by the basketful.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Climbing perch
riverSoutheastAsia.note: Said to climb trees. It can at least cross mud on its gill spines.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Giant gourami
riverSoutheastAsia.note: Breathes air and builds a nest of water plants.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Snakehead
riverSoutheastAsia.note: Breathes air and can live for days out of water.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Clown knifefish
riverSoutheastAsia.note: Flat as a blade, with a row of dark spots like portholes.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Freshwater prawn
riverSoutheastAsia.note: A giant river prawn with long, blue claws.

riverSoutheastAsia.name: Giant catfish
riverSoutheastAsia.note: Bigger than a man and seen only a few times a year.

riverAfrica.name: Tilapia
riverAfrica.note: Keeps its eggs and young safe in its mouth.

riverAfrica.name: African catfish
riverAfrica.note: Can breathe air and live for days in damp mud.

riverAfrica.name: Elephantfish
riverAfrica.note: Its long nose feels the mud, and it talks to its kind in faint electric pulses.

riverAfrica.name: Bichir
riverAfrica.note: Has lungs and armoured scales. Its family is older than the dinosaurs.

riverAfrica.name: Freshwater crab
riverAfrica.note: Lives far from the sea, in burrows along the riverbank.

riverAfrica.name: Tigerfish
riverAfrica.note: Interlocking teeth like a dog's. It leaps the moment it's hooked.

riverAfrica.name: Nile perch
riverAfrica.note: Huge and silver, and a fight to get to the bank.

riverAustralia.name: Golden perch
riverAustralia.note: Swims hundreds of kilometres upriver after a flood.

riverAustralia.name: Catfish
riverAustralia.note: The eel-tailed catfish builds a round nest of gravel.

riverAustralia.name: Eel
riverAustralia.note: The Gunditjmara farmed them in stone channels for thousands of years.

riverAustralia.name: Yabby
riverAustralia.note: Dug out of muddy banks or coaxed up on a string with meat.

riverAustralia.name: Barramundi
riverAustralia.note: Explodes from the water when hooked, gill plates rattling.

riverAustralia.name: Murray cod
riverAustralia.note: Ponde, the great cod that carved out the Murray River in the old story.

riverAmazon.name: Pacu
riverAmazon.note: Has teeth like a person's, for cracking nuts that fall in the water.

riverAmazon.name: Piranha
riverAmazon.note: Its jaw full of teeth was used as a pair of scissors.

riverAmazon.name: Catfish
riverAmazon.note: A red-tailed catfish, all mouth and whiskers.

riverAmazon.name: Peacock bass
riverAmazon.note: Hits hard and fights like a much bigger fish.

riverAmazon.name: Tambaqui
riverAmazon.note: Eats fruit that falls into the flooded forest.

riverAmazon.name: Freshwater stingray
riverAmazon.note: Lies buried in the sand. Shuffle your feet when you wade.

riverAmazon.name: Electric eel
riverAmazon.note: Can stun a horse. Humboldt watched it happen in 1800.

riverAmazon.name: Arapaima
riverAmazon.note: Rises every few minutes to gulp air. Its tongue was used as a grater.

lakeMexico.name: Charal
lakeMexico.note: Tiny silver fish netted by the thousand and dried in the sun.

lakeMexico.name: White fish
lakeMexico.note: Pescado blanco, so pale you can almost see through it.

lakeMexico.name: Acocil
lakeMexico.note: Little lake crayfish, eaten with chile and lime.

lakeMexico.name: Axolotl
lakeMexico.note: Never grows up and keeps its frilly gills for life. Roasted in Tenochtitlan.

lakeMexico.name: Goodeid
lakeMexico.note: Gives birth to live young, unlike most fish.

lakeAndes.name: Ispi
lakeAndes.note: Tiny silver fish, fried whole by the plateful.

lakeAndes.name: Carachi
lakeAndes.note: A little killifish of Titicaca, dried in the sun by the thousand.

lakeAndes.name: Boga
lakeAndes.note: Swims in open water out past the reed beds.

lakeAndes.name: Lake frog
lakeAndes.note: A huge, baggy-skinned frog that never leaves the lake.

lakeAndes.name: Suche
lakeAndes.note: A spotted catfish that hides in the totora reeds.
